A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures and complete appendices. Content can be matched despite the revised layout and appendix/figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SGD/reg-SGD simulations for tomography, a two-dimensional toy problem and an ODE inverse problem, including repeated-run results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds initial-step-size sensitivity results in Appendix A.2, Figures 10–11.

M1.justification: Equations (3)–(4) and Algorithm 1 retain the same gradient update with decaying Tikhonov regularization. The new finite-sum example formalizes an existing gradient-estimation setting rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate tomography reconstruction, the same two-variable toy objective and the same linear ODE inverse problem. The added initial-step-size sweep changes configurations within the existing toy task.

E2.justification: The evaluated methods remain vanilla SGD and reg-SGD, including the existing alternative regularization schedules. The added sensitivity study uses these same methods; newly cited algorithms are not added as empirical comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a sweep over initial step sizes {0.01, 0.1, 1, 2}, using alpha_k=alpha_1*k^(-1/2) for SGD and alpha_k=alpha_1*k^(-0.667), lambda_k=k^(-0.111) for reg-SGD. Each trajectory has 10^7 iterations. Settings for matched earlier experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 10–11 isolate sensitivity to the initial step-size multiplier while fixing the decay exponents. This supplements the retained analysis varying regularization and step-size decay exponents.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain their run counts and reporting practices: 100-run averages in Figure 6 and individual trajectories with averages across 10 runs in the pathwise studies. The new sensitivity plots use the existing 10-run practice without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds optimality-gap and minimum-norm squared-error curves for the initial-step-size sweep. These show differing transients and persistent SGD minimum-norm error versus declining reg-SGD error under their respective schedules. All previously reported experiment graphics are retained unchanged after matching renumbering.

T1.justification: v2 adds Example 1.3 and a finite-sum variance-bound proof in Lemma C.1. It generalizes the convergence corollary to allow summable multiplicative perturbations and revises the main convergence proofs. Theorem D.7 changes its boundary condition from 2*C_lambda*C_alpha>beta to >min(beta,1-q), with corresponding rescaling. Appendix E also corrects squared-error source bounds from lambda and lambda^(2nu) to lambda^2 and lambda^nu, respectively. These are substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The headline convergence, minimum-norm selection, stability and rate claims remain unchanged. However, Section 1.3 narrows the novelty framing: v1 identifies only one prior discrete-time treatment, whereas v2 acknowledges established iterative regularization methods and positions its extension specifically in stochastic discrete time.

C2.justification: v2 relates its summability requirement to the Attouch–Czarnecki condition in Appendix D.2 and explicitly links source conditions to the Łojasiewicz refinement in Appendix E. The conclusion adds tangential-cone assumptions as a possible route beyond convexity. Existing experimental interpretations and principal limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 documents the added sensitivity study's initial step sizes, decay schedules and iteration budget. Implementation details for the existing tomography, toy and ODE experiments remain unchanged, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 and new Appendix D.2.1 substantially expand positioning around iterative regularization, modified Landweber methods, hierarchical optimization, penalty-based variational inclusions and inverse-problem SGD. The single-predecessor framing is replaced by explicit connections to older literature, including Bakushinsky, Attouch–Czarnecki, Scherzer and Jin and collaborators.

P1.justification: The revision expands related-work exposition, inserts a finite-sum appendix, subdivides the deterministic-analysis discussion and makes local terminology, cross-reference and acknowledgment edits. Most of the abstract, main narrative, theorem exposition and experimental descriptions retain their earlier wording and organization.

P2.justification: A document-wide template change revises typography, title and author arrangement, spacing, figure scale and placement. v2 adds Figures 10–11 and reverses the order of the earlier Figures 8–9. Existing graphics are reused, but the overall visual layout is substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 improves research positioning, corrects source-condition exponents, addresses proof gaps and adds sensitivity evidence. However, new Lemma C.1 introduces an invalid average-smoothness bound: for M=1, x=1 and f_i(x)=L_i*x^2/2 with L_i=(1,0.01,0.01,0.01), its stated assumptions give noise variance 0.18376875, exceeding the claimed bound 0.1326125. The benefits therefore coexist with a new mathematical error, making the net quality direction uncertain.
